item.title: The Sun unleashed a monster storm. Earth may have made it worse
item.description:
Waypoint is curating and commenting on third-party reporting. Original publisher: ScienceDaily.
Summary: The massive solar storm that illuminated skies worldwide in May 2024 has uncovered an unexpected twist: Earth's own atmosphere may have helped make the storm so powerful. Satellite measurements revealed that roughly 85% of the charged particles fueling the disturbance originated from Earth's upper atmosphere rather than the solar wind.
Waypoint’s Take: For someone heading outside, the useful question is observational: use the report as a planning signal — precipitation, wind, and visibility change what is safe and worth noticing. Keep the publisher’s claims provisional until you read the original. If you go out, pair the story with current Dashboard readings rather than the headline alone.
Read the original article at the publisher: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261111005905.htm
